title: Vanishing of one section descends on a fixed affine chart
statement: Let $I$ be a directed preorder, $R:I\to\mathrm{CRing}$ a diagram, and $c$ a limiting cone of the inverse diagram of spectra with affine vertex $S$ [def-pc-scheme]. Fix $i\leq j$ and a morphism $f:X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$. Put $X_j=X_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}\operatorname{Spec}(R_j)$, with projection $p_j$, and $X=X_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}S$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $G$ be a quasi-coherent module of finite presentation on $X_j$ [pqf-def-coherent]. Fix an affine open $U\subseteq X_i$ and $y\in\Gamma(p_j^{-1}(U),G)$. Supply a tensor-pullback/pushforward adjunction for $X\to X_j$ and one for each $X_k\to X_j$ with $j\leq k$ [def-pc-module-pullback, lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. If the limit adjunction unit sends $y$ to zero, there is $l\geq j$ such that, for every $k\geq l$, the unit of the supplied stage adjunction sends $y$ to zero. The bound depends on this single section; no source module or module morphism is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the one-stage affine section vanishing theorem to get l ≥ j with zero unit at l. Apply persistence of zero sections under further base change to every k ≥ l. The finite-presentation assumption is not needed.
